# PPPlayer: Complete Product Information

PPPlayer is a free, cross-platform, open-source media player designed for discovery, seamless streaming, and high-fidelity local media playback.

## Repositories & License
- **App Repository**: https://github.com/ppplayer-labs/app (Flutter/Dart)
- **Website Repository**: https://github.com/ppplayer-labs/website (Next.js)
- **License**: MIT License
- **Current Version**: See latest release on GitHub

## Privacy & Account Requirements
- **Account Requirements**: None. PPPlayer is completely free and does not require subscriptions, accounts, emails, or sign-ups to use any features.
- **Privacy & Data Collection**: PPPlayer's privacy policy explicitly states that no personal information (names, emails, payment info, precise location) is collected. However, to improve stability, the app does collect anonymous usage analytics (feature usage, session duration), crash reports, error logs, and basic device/OS metadata.

## Playback Features
- **Core Playback**: Supports audio/video streaming, local media playback, subtitles, M3U network streams, playlists, artist discovery, infinite artist radio, and related artists exploration.
- **Platform Integration**: Picture-in-Picture (PiP), background playback and system controls depend on platform and source. The development iOS build forwards both native and WebKit system play/pause commands to explicit playback intent.

## Current Release — PPPlayer 4.0.0 (October 15, 2026)

PPPlayer 4.0.0 is the current production release (Application: 4.0.0+12, Windows MSIX: 4.0.0.0, Publisher: Devflier). Published assets include Android (Google Play, APK, AAB), macOS (DMG, ZIP; Apple Developer ID signed & notarized), Windows (Microsoft Store, MSIX direct), and Linux (Snap Store `sudo snap install ppplayer`, AppImage, Debian package, portable tarball).

Supported Platform Requirements:
- macOS: macOS 13.0 or newer, Apple Silicon & Intel (Universal).
- Windows: Windows 10 or later (64-bit x64).
- Android: Android 7.0 (API 24) or newer (ARM64, x86_64).
- Linux: Modern 64-bit distributions (Ubuntu 20.04+, Debian 11+, Fedora, Arch).
- iOS: iOS 15.0 or newer (in development).

Key 4.0.0 Features:
- Chromium YouTube routing on Android, macOS, Windows, and Linux with native player integration; iOS retains WebKit. Local media and direct network streams use MediaKit.
- Redesigned queue interface with resizable desktop sidebar, mobile bottom sheet, independent fullscreen browsing, and persisted width preference.
- Comprehensive network playlist support: M3U, PLS, XSPF, and ASX parsing, automatic HLS stream classification, IPTV header/group grouping, relative URL resolution, and bounded HTTP reads.
- Robust local-library handling with schema 14 migration, durable media relinking, metadata extraction, and video probing.
- Corrected playback recovery, source switching, and macOS graceful Quit handshake with zero orphaned Chromium helpers.
- First-class Linux packaging supporting Snap Store (`sudo snap install ppplayer`), standalone AppImage, Debian (.deb), and portable tarball.

Known Limitations:
- Android YouTube background playback when the screen is turned off is unsupported in this version (YouTube iframe policy compliance and platform power management). Local and direct media playback in the background remains fully supported.

Releases & Assets: https://github.com/ppplayer-labs/app/releases

## Earlier playback work (historical development notes, October 2, 2026)

These features are in development and do not imply inclusion in current public downloads or public iOS availability.

- **Durable iOS music imports**: New imports are managed copies that remain available after reopening. Old entries pointing to deleted temporary files require reimporting the originals.
- **Play On**: In-app iOS AirPlay picker with active receiver name and selection. On macOS, Play On opens Sound settings and displays the system default output name and route changes via Core Audio. The macOS shortcut changes system routing, not an app-only receiver session. AirPlay uses the local engine and Apple routing, not LocalMediaServer.
- **Network outputs**: Cast backends exist for Android/iOS; DLNA depends on platform capabilities. iOS DLNA discovery requires approved multicast capability and an enabled build configuration. YouTube is not supported through the Cast/DLNA media-URL handoff.
- **Local file serving**: Apple security-scoped bookmarks resolve at file acquisition, and authorized file leases remain active while accepted HTTP reads finish. Cast/DLNA receivers must support the source format; PPPlayer does not transcode.
- **Player layout**: Dedicated Queue button, responsive video controls and secondary options menu. Local audio displays its own artwork or fallback instead of stale video thumbnails.
- **iPhone system pause**: WebKit media-session actions reach Flutter intent; explicit pause cancels recovery, while background recovery remains available for involuntary pauses.
- **Validation**: Physical iPhone-to-MacBook local-music AirPlay and iPhone system pause/play were checked. Automated local-file-to-fake-Cast HTTP handoff passed. Physical Chromecast and DLNA validation remain pending.
- **Guide**: https://ppplayer.com/blog/play-on-local-files-ios (English); https://ppplayer.com/pt-BR/blog/play-on-local-files-ios (Brazilian Portuguese).

## Supported Platforms and Availability
- **Android**: Verified public listing on Google Play (`https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.ppplayer.app`). Direct APK downloads available via GitHub Releases.
- **Windows**: Verified public listing on the Microsoft Store (`https://apps.microsoft.com/store/detail/9NKNDF67BG4X`).
- **macOS**: Available via direct DMG download on GitHub Releases.
- **Linux**: Experimental support.
*(Note: iOS TestFlight and App Store availability claims have been removed as there are no verified public URLs).*

## Localization & Language Support
The website routes and application support **38 corresponding locales**. New playback-update editorial content is available in English and Brazilian Portuguese, with English fallback for other website locales. This does not imply that every article or newly added feature description has been translated into all languages.

### Website
The website is explicitly configured to support **38 languages**:
English (`en`), Arabic (`ar`), Bengali (`bn`), Czech (`cs`), Danish (`da`), Dutch (`nl`), German (`de`), Spanish (`es`), Estonian (`et`), Persian (`fa`), Filipino (`fil`), French (`fr`), Guarani (`gn`), Hindi (`hi`), Croatian (`hr`), Hungarian (`hu`), Indonesian (`id`), Italian (`it`), Japanese (`ja`), Georgian (`ka`), Kazakh (`kk`), Korean (`ko`), Latvian (`lv`), Malay (`ms`), Burmese (`my`), Nigerian Pidgin (`pcm`), Polish (`pl`), Brazilian Portuguese (`pt-BR`), Romanian (`ro`), Russian (`ru`), Swedish (`sv`), Thai (`th`), Turkish (`tr`), Ukrainian (`uk`), Urdu (`ur`), Uzbek (`uz`), Vietnamese (`vi`), and Chinese (`zh`).

### Flutter App (Upcoming Release)
The application generates and supports all **38 corresponding languages** at runtime:
- **Selectable in App Settings (38 languages)**: Users can manually select any of the 38 languages (plus "System Default") from the settings menu. 
- **Parity Note**: The app uses `pt` for Brazilian Portuguese, corresponding to the website's `pt-BR`.
